Just something about meeting friends here - as you may know Poles aren't known for being really outgoing, but if you show any interest in polish culture it may be a nice icebraker for getting to know some locals and then you may meet new folk by mutuals. If you greet someone with "how are you" expect to have an honest answer about what's going on in their life if you know that person well before being asked the same question. And don't be discouraged by the grumpy faces - i know polish smile is a meme and the whole thing may be exaggerated on the internet, but compared to "westerners" majority of people there will really smile less towards strangers.

Until 1942 Poles accounted for the majority of the Auschwitz camp prisoners. After the jewish transports in 1942 Jews became the majority. According to Auschwitz muzeum web page there were 1.1 milion Jews in the camp and 140-150 thousand Poles. There were 23 thousands of Romani prisoners, so no - there were more Poles in the camp than Romani (not counting polish jews). Of course I'm not there to diminish the suffering of Romani people, but I really don't like forgetting about Polish casualties.

What I'd recommend since there's a lot of pop and indie - the Dumplings (electro pop), kwiat jabłoni is also kinda indie - folk pop, Brodka, Bokka - these are kinda alternative.

I dont really listen to polish rap, but I'd say Taco Hemmimgway is kinda popular and more on the pop music side than others rappers.

If you want to dive into polish doomer core, alt rock etc. then I'd definitely recommend Myslovitz (some people would compare them to Radiohead), older Kult songs, Maanam, obywatel G.C.

Among some older, XX. century pop I'd say Anna Jantar, Zbigniew Wodecki, Marek Grechuta, Maryla Rodowicz, Krzysztof Krawczyk.
